newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU THROWS FIVE MORE SCORELESS INNINGS IN MINORS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU THROWS FIVE MORE SCORELESS INNINGS IN MINORS.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu continued his whitewashing of minor-league batters Friday when he threw five innings of scoreless ball in his latest stop en route to the New York Yankees.

Irabu, who signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the Yankees in late May, yielded just four hits, two of them infield scratch singles, and got the victory in the AA Eastern League Norwich Navigators' 8-0 win over the New Haven Ravens.
He gave up no walks, as in his previous two wins in Class-A ball, and notched five strikeouts with a balk.
The 28-year-old right-hander threw 24 pitches clocked over 90 mph (145 kph), the fastest at 96 mph (155 kph). Of 67 pitches, 48 were strikes.

Irabu gave credit to longtime Yankee pitching coach Billy Conners. "There is tremendous pressure but through the accumulation of workouts under Billy Connors I was successful," he said through an interpreter.
"I had a problem with the mound because of the difference in the angle of the mound. I am happy with my performance."
"This is his third outing on the way to the big leagues," Connors said. "He has great command of his pitches. When the man got on second, he showed you what he's made of, and got out of it."

With one out in the fourth inning, Derrick Gibson doubled on a hanging curve ball, but Irabu struck out the next two batters swinging to snuff out the threat. After giving up a leadoff single in the fifth, Irabu struck out the next three batters.
Irabu is expected to pitch for Columbus, the Yankees' top minor-league team, before reaching the major leagues sometime around the July All-Star break.

The Yankees acquired Irabu through a deal with the San Diego Padres, who owned his rights through an agreement with his Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines. Irabu had said he would not play for anyone but the Yankees in Major League Baseball.
